subject: Music Production
title: Tinnitus and the Producer's Curse
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Tinnitus and the Producer's Curse.

hook.text: Many musicians hear a constant ringing in their ears even when the room is completely silent.

buildup.text: Tinnitus occurs when damaged hair cells send phantom signals to the brain without any real sound.

discovery.text: The brain interprets these false signals as a persistent tone that never stops.

twist.text: Beethoven likely suffered tinnitus, composing his greatest works while hearing phantom noise.

climax.text: Modern producers use reference tracks and careful volume to minimize their tinnitus risk.

punchline.text: A sound that doesn't exist haunts damaged ears.

quiz.question: What causes tinnitus?
options: Excess ear wax blocking the canal
Damaged hair cells sending phantom signals
Listening to too many frequencies at once
